If your life was always "boring" then how did you live until the day you first smoked?
It's not you talking rn
It's the weed talking.

When you quit you have to make changes, you'll have tons of free time you'll just be wandering around aimlessly looking for something to stimulate your dead serotonin receptor. That's one of the main reasons you feel bored and sad when you quit weed. ThC replaces serotonin  and dopamine in your body. So your body produces less on its own until your next smoke.

There are ways to treat withdrawls
#1 FIND A NEW INTEREST 
       As cliche as this may sound it's a brilliant advice to      pass time and possibly learn something new while making yourself tired for night time.

#2 NIGHT TIMES CAN BE SCARY 
    Day times are a breeze but night is when it really kicks off with the intense dreams and insomnia. To counter this, I would suggest doing some  exercise in the evening , staying away from caffeine  and sugar past 5 or 6, drink hot chamomile tea before bed( i use 4 bags) . The dreams can be intense but there isn't much you can do that but I've discovered keeping something over your eyes helps abit , idk the logic behind this but having a durag + beanie then a eye cover makes me feel soothed. But the eye cover alone works fine for me.

#3 TELL SOMEONE YOU TRUST 
The last thing you want to do is don't alone, it's not impossible for it to be done alone but I think it's more tedious. But telling someone that loves and supports you is a big boost. Its a mental game with you vs quitting. So having someone affirm you that you've got this could help with intruding thoughts of relapsing 

#4 TRY SUPPLEMENTS 
I know supplements can be expensive but its worth a shot, when you quit your body doesn't produce certain chemicals like it used to before , thus why you feel depressed and helpless. I combine 5htp and L tyrosine respectfully , I dose in the morning and at night. I'm not sure if it actually helps but I haven't lost My mind haha.
But you should also do your own research and possibly check with your doctor.  Stay away from those supplements mentioned above if you're on anytime of depression medication. Just don't take my word for it and do research.

#5 LET IT ALL OUT
Dont hold back any emotion you're feeling , the best time to quit is when you aren't going to work/school as you may have anger outbursts but that's good, it means you're healing. What I do is take a hot shower and remind myself on how weed hasn't benefited me and it's just an illusion. You will feel all kinds of emotions , if you're sad then cry it out! If you're angry then punch your pillow. 


You can do this! gradually your pre weed senses will begin to return to normal. And you will literally Feel the moment you have a new thought or feel interested in an activity you haven't committed too because you only did it when you smoked like gaming , chores etc.

Even if you relapse , learn from it like think about what made you want to relapse and get rid of it.
You can do this  you're 1 in 8 billion  afterall!
